headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from ctx’s MCP/browser/file surfaces; LightZero is local-only and non-writing, limiting conflict and leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem and browser surfaces, so attacker-controlled content could be routed into its context. LightZero has no MCP, filesystem write, or browser capability, so the bridge is one-way and not a shared channel. The interaction is plausible in default developer workflows, but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF ctx is connected to Claude Code event hooks during active tool use, then injected content can reach ctx context.
IF LightZero remains non-MCP and non-browser as profiled, it cannot originate a direct shared-channel injection path.
mitigations: Disable ctx hooks for untrusted sessions.
Restrict ctx to a dedicated workspace with no attacker-controlled files.
Require manual review before ctx forwards any observed content into prompts.
Run LightZero in a separate process boundary with no shared clipboard or filesystem.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all hook-derived content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, while LightZero is profiled as read/write isolated with no filesystem access, network egress, or MCP use. That makes shared-workspace leakage unlikely from the pair as described. Because LightZero has no data classes touched and no read surface, the main risk is limited to ctx-side logging rather than cross-agent exfiltration.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external harness that injects secrets into its prompts, ctx logs could capture them.
IF ctx is configured to persist audit/runtime logs containing sensitive workspace content, leakage scope increases.
mitigations: Store ctx logs in a redacted sink.
Keep sensitive files out of ctx-observed directories.
Run LightZero without shared workspace mounts.
Rotate or delete runtime logs after each session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and install packages, but LightZero is explicitly unable to write files, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping write authority on the same mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the relevant write surfaces are documented on both sides.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants LightZero write or git permissions not shown in the profile, conflict severity increases.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory through a wrapper, file clobbering becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Deny LightZero any write-capable wrapper permissions.
Serialize ctx package installs during maintenance windows.
Use read-only mounts for LightZero inputs.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or transactional writes for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a harness that observes tool events and can surface graph/runtime data, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. LightZero is a game-playing agent with no verification or action-taking safeguards shown, so if its outputs are fed into ctx-driven workflows, errors can cascade into incorrect records or decisions. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are consumed by ctx without an explicit verification step, cascading error risk is present.
IF ctx forwards observed results into logs or downstream automation, mistaken game-state facts can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ctx acts on LightZero outputs.
Require schema validation on all LightZero-derived messages.
Mark LightZero outputs as untrusted in ctx prompts.
Limit downstream actions to read-only reporting.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data, which can create compliance obligations, while LightZero lists no data classes touched and no network egress. Because no concrete mismatch is documented, this is a low-severity compliance watch item rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF ctx logs contain regulated data classes, retention and deletion controls must be applied.
IF LightZero is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter logging rules than ctx’s storage location, a policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Review log-retention settings for ctx.
Avoid placing regulated data in ctx-observed paths.
Document the storage region for any ctx logs.
Keep LightZero inputs free of regulated data.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
